actions.spoken: Hi. Welcome to MADHAV Order Desk, a working prototype for small businesses taking orders through chat. Let me show you how the owner stays in control.
Here's Aanya. She asks for one chocolate cake tomorrow, in Hinglish, and wants to know the price. Nothing is booked yet.
I click Prepare reply. This recording uses Sample mode, so this step is not a live AI request. The demo correctly identifies the product, quantity, and pickup date.
The price comes from the bakery catalog. Nine hundred rupees total, and four hundred and fifty in suggested advance. I can still review the details before accepting.
Only when I approve and reserve does that order enter the system. The confirmation draft updates after reservation.
I approve the reply separately. The message now appears in the simulated chat. No real WhatsApp message was sent.
Here is Aanya's order in the order book. Nine hundred rupees in order value, and no payment recorded yet.
Rohan wants Red Velvet. But the bakery has no capacity for this cake. What happens when a customer asks for something we cannot make?
MADHAV blocks the booking, and lists available alternatives including Vanilla Cloud. It asks the customer to decide, instead of secretly changing the order.
Now Rohan replies, Kal one vanilla cake kar do. I'm adding that as a new fictional customer message.
We prepare the updated request. Vanilla Cloud is available at seven hundred and fifty rupees. This is the order we can safely review and reserve.
I approve the vanilla reservation and then the reply. Red Velvet was never booked.
Next is Meera. She wants two boxes of cupcakes for tomorrow, and we need to keep the order amount separate from money actually received.
Each box is four hundred and twenty rupees. Two boxes come to eight hundred and forty. The owner reviews the price and quantity before booking.
The order is now approved, and so is the reply. That still doesn't mean the customer has paid.
In the Orders screen, Meera's total is eight hundred and forty. Payment recording requires the owner to confirm it independently.
Suppose I've verified four hundred and twenty rupees received. I'll enter that amount now, then confirm it.
The remaining balance is four hundred and twenty rupees. Notice how the order total, paid amount and outstanding balance stay consistent.

That's MADHAV: checked order preparation, catalog-based pricing, capacity protection, and owner approval. This is a WhatsApp-style simulation, not a real WhatsApp integration. Next we plan to test with small businesses and build the official integration.
